title: Turn-Taking and Pairs
welcome_lead: Pick up the analyst's microscope: turns, adjacency pairs and floor management — the atoms of conversation.
meta_desc: Turn-taking, adjacency pairs and floor management as A-Level discourse analysis tools.
final_note: You have stocked the analyst's toolkit — turn allocation, adjacency pairs, transitions and floor mechanics.

concepts.def: A speaker's contribution between TRPs; the basic unit of conversational structure.
Mechanisms for assigning the next turn — current speaker selects next, or next self-selects.
The right to speak at a given moment; speakers compete for and yield the floor.
Two speakers talking simultaneously, often at a TRP (incidental) or in interruption (competitive).
Immediate uptake of the next turn with no gap or overlap — tight conversational fit.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sacks, Schegloff and Jefferson's 1974 system uses two rules: at a TRP the current speaker may select the next, or any other participant may self-select.

The mechanism predicts very small gaps and overlaps in real talk — coordination without explicit instructions.

Adjacency pairs create normative expectations. After a question, an answer is normatively due; silence is heard as significant.

Inserted sequences (an insertion sequence between first and second pair-parts) allow clarification without breaking the pair.

Speakers hold the floor through projectable syntax, gaze and prosody; they yield by completing a TCU and looking at the next speaker.

Skilled speakers exploit these signals to manage long turns or invite contributions.
